# dsh-session-batch
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds a sidebar panel for **deleting the chat records of many co
nversations at once**, optionally **together with the files each conversation produced**, and that r
eports an **honest session status**: actually running versus merely kept in host memory.
> Deletion is permanent. Nothing goes to a recycle bin.
## Why this exists
The harness ships archive, not delete: the persistence seam deliberately offers no removal API, so s
ession logs accumulate under `$DSH_HOME/sessions` forever. And its sidebar cannot tell you why a con
versation looks "in use" — a session that was merely *opened once* stays in host memory for the life
of the process, which no page refresh clears.
Artifact attribution — working out which workspace files a conversation actually produced — is a sep
arate, much harder problem, and `dsh-session-artifacts` already solves it well (create-only evidence
, per-command time windows, cross-session uniqueness, DSH-home and package fences). This plugin does
**not** re-implement any of that. When that plugin is installed, this one delegates to its exported
functions verbatim.
## Features
- **Batch deletion of chat records** — tick any number of conversations in one panel and delete them
in a single request: session logs, subagent records, workspace membership, pin and archive markers.
- **Optional artifact removal** — one checkbox in the confirm dialog deletes the files those conver
sations produced, including files produced by their subagent sessions. The list and total size are s

hown before anything is removed.
- **Honest status badges** — `Running` (a turn, owned jobs, subagen
ts or scheduled reminders are active, read from the harness' own `workspace/session-activity` waterf
all) versus `In memory` (the host still holds the Session object; refreshing will not change it, res

tarting the app will).
- **Deletion that can be trusted** — every log directory is verified gone on
disk, a running session that refuses to stop aborts the whole operation with zero side effects, purg
ed ids are tombstoned so the panel agrees with reality, and anything that could not be removed is qu
eued and retried on the next start.
## Requirements
- DSH `0.2.x` with the `connection`, `sessionQuery` and `workspaceRegistry` services (every shipped

web composition has them).
- Optional: `dsh-session-artifacts` `>= 0.7.0` for artifact removal. With
out it the artifact checkbox is hidden and only chat records are deleted.

The Desktop shell owns its profile exclusively, so `dsh plugin` refuses to touch it. `scripts/instal
l-when-closed.ps1` performs the swap while the app is closed and verifies the result:

It edits the profile manifest, runs the bundled pnpm, force-syncs the runtime files, checks their SH
A-256 against the source, and restarts the app. `scripts/rollback-when-closed.ps1` reverts to the ma
nifest it backed up.
## Usage

1. Open **Batch purge** in the sidebar.
2. Press **Select**, tick conversations (or use *Select all*

— logs, subagent records, workspace membership.

4. C
onfirm. Single conversations can be deleted from their own row without entering selection mode.
## How deletion works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **Stop first.** `workspace/session-activity` is asked whether the session does work; if it does, `
workspace/session-stop` is invoked and the answer is polled for up to 8 seconds. Still busy? The pur

ge is refused and **nothing** is touched.
- **Remove artifacts first**, while the logs still exist t
o attribute from. Each session in the group (root and every subagent) is asked separately through `d

sh-session-artifacts`; the union is deduped by path.
- **Verify the logs are gone.** A session held
in host memory can recreate its directory right after a successful `rm`, so the removal is re-checke
d on disk and retried up to four times. Whatever still comes back is queued in `$DSH_HOME/session-ba

tch/pending.json` and retried on the next start — files by path, since by then the log is gone.

## Compatibility matrix
| Resource | this plugin | dsh-session-artifacts |

| Sidebar panel | `sidebar.panellist` id `session-batch`, `main` key `session-batch` | none |
| Sess

ion row menu | unused | `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` id `dsh-session-artifacts.delete` |
|
Host services | `connection`, `sessionQuery`, `workspaceRegistry` | `webServer`, `sessionPersistenc
| `connection`, `sessionQuery`, `workspaceRegistry` | `webServer`, `sessionPersistence`, `agents` |
No slot or service is contested, so both can be installed together. The only overlap is that both ca
n remove a session record; whichever runs first wins and the other finds nothing to do.
## What is never deleted

- Files a conversation only **delivered** (`present` without creating them).
- Files it merely **edi

ted or rewrote**.
- Files that fall inside another session's command window too (ambiguous → claimed

by neither).
- Anything under `$DSH_HOME`.
These are `dsh-session-artifacts`' rules, inherited by delegation, and they are deliberate: a conver
sation that handed you a file you already owned must not make that file disposable.
## Known limitations
- A Session that was already open cannot be released — the harness exposes no release call. Deleting
such a conversation removes its log immediately and hides its row here, but the harness' **own** si

debar keeps the row until the app restarts.
- Retro-attribution needs the log. Once a log is gone, i

ts queued files can only be retried by path.
- The batch cap is 200 sessions per request.
- Deleting
from a second browser tab that still has the conversation open can recreate the log; close it first
from a second browser tab that still has the conversation open can recreate the log; close it first.
